recipes.name: Zucchini Delight
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can canned peeled and diced tomatoes

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Slice zucchini and onion and place in a glass dish baking dish. Add can of tomatoes, salt and pepper. Sprinkle cheese over top. Place lid on dish.
Bake in the preheated 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) until zucchini becomes tender, 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Delight
raw_recipe.description: This is a quick and healthy dish. Great in the summer when zucchini is in season! Sound too easy to be good? Try it!

review.reviewBody: I have been making this for years , but I do mine in the frying pan and I add ground beef and cumin and garlic for more flavor. Then I eat it with tortillas.

Very good. I used a 10 oz can of Mexican tomatoes cuz that’s all I had. Then added a little water and 3 Tbs of tomato paste. I sautéed the onions first, as someone recommended. We are vegan so I used vegan Mexican cheese on top, added the the last 5 minutes and it did take 45 overall.
I sautee the onion first along with a clove or two of minced garlic. I also increased the cheese to 3/4 cup and added crumbled bacon. OMG! So good.

A very sturdy base recipe. Tasted very good even after some fussing on my end (doubled the amount of tomatoes, added an extra zucchini, accidentally added several times as much cheese, and the only planned change: Added basil and oregano to taste - had to cook 40 minutes instead of 20 due to using too small of a baking dish. Mistakes were made. Delicious, delicious mistakes.) and from what I could tell would be perfectly good without any modifications. The fact that is could stand up to so many mild mistakes on my end and still be tasty shows it's a recipe you've got leeway with, too, which makes it something I feel would be easy for beginners.

It has a light, summery feel, and tasted wonderful when paired with a greek feta spinach salad and a spinach Florentine quiche. Would also pair amazingly with grilled salmon instead of quiche. 

Will be making this again in the future.

This was a pretty good side dish. It served 5 of us as a side. I layered the zucchini and onions then added the tomatoes on top. I would recommend draining the tomatoes because it had a lot of liquid in it by the time it was done cooking. I used canned tomatoes with basil, garlic and oregano. And used provolone cheese, its what I had on hand. Thanks for the recipe.

Fabulous- Build like lasagne, sprinkle with the onions, season and sprinkle with parmesan, layer by layer; the top layer is complete after straining the juice from seasoned diced tomatoes and dividing over top, there is lots of cheese and my additional touch- seasoned bread crumbs

I made this tonight. I read others review a used the Italian diced tomatoes. This was tasty however I would drain the tomatoes next time. I added the cheese for the last 10 minutes as others suggested with the lid off. add italian seasoning to your zucchini/onion mixture and drain the tomatoes and it is good.

Ok I did make changes but only because I didn't have the exact ingredients on hand. I used diced tomatos and added an extra can of rotel HOT diced tomatos in addition because only one 15 oz can didn't look like enough. And I thought I probably added a whole cup of cheddar cheese as I just eyed it to be sure it was nicely covered with sprinkled cheese. I also cooked it 30min because my zucchini was a LARGE one. And even at that, it was still crunchy, but frankly, I loved the crunchiness of it! I also added my beloved spice garlic powder! I added the salt, pepper and garlic powder over the whole thing at the end rather than throughout. It needed no extra spice after that! I used a 9x13 glass pan.

I saute the onions first and partially cook the zucchini on the stovetop or in the microwave until slightly tender. I use fresh tomatoes. Layer the zucchini, onions, tomatoes adding salt and pepper on the onion layer. Then put in the oven uncovered for 20 min. adding the cheese the last 5 min. Delicious!

I used red onion and fresh tomatoes (with the juices and seeds) and a bit of vegetable juice because I didn't have canned tomatoes. I added garlic powder, anchovy paste and a dash of cayenne for a kick of flavor. Then I threw in some fresh basil because its the last growth of the season on my plant. I was out of cheese but didn't want it anyway, turned out pretty good! Great way to use up vegetables!

As is it lacks flavor. My version is to use mexi or italian herbed canned tomatoes and mozzerella cheese. Both are very good but I prefer the spicy one.I dont normally use onions in this unless I carmelize them first.If you do this in a pan and get it all(Zuke too)browned a bit it has more flavor. Then top with cheese and broil til brown and bubbly.Yum!
Made just as shown

Like some of the other reviewers, I didn’t enjoy it. It lacked flavor and took way longer than 20 minutes to bake. I ended up sautéing it in a pan with olive oil & garlic. Also, it’s probably best to drain most of the liquid from the canned tomatoes.
Made just as written. Loved it. Will be using this during zucchini harvest, yum!
It’s is really delicious.

I followed the recipe except I used stewed tomatoes and added Italian seasoning and garlic powder on top. I covered and baked 35 minutes. It was good and didn't take long to make. I will make it again.
No seasoning at all. I would not make it again.
If you don't want vegetarian, try some habanero cheese and hot Italian sausage.

I used one large zucchini and 2 cups of cheese. Wished my dish was more spread out. The bowl shape required 5 min. more of cook time. I'll try again with some added meat or mushrooms. I didn't feel like the onions were cooked enough.
Watery and bland. I love zucchini and couldn't even finish this. Will not make again.
